transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-01
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Carlos Reyes (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (CTO, Veridian), Daniel Ruiz (SRE, Veridian), Lena Cho (PM, Veridian)
Links shared: https://redwood.app/ops/rca-notes-aug28.pdf, spreadsheet: https://redwood.app/ops/latency-traces-aug28.csv

Summary:
Quick lab-style session to recon the recent production degradation on 2025-08-28 (spike in tail latency and token duplication when KV cache warmed) and agree a hardened canary + deployment checklist. Focus was on reproducing the KV-cache divergence, clarifying SLO thresholds, and confirming security/compliance gating for a private canary run.

Topics:
- Repro steps for KV cache mismatch
- Deployment guardrails (fallback policy, circuit breaker thresholds)
- Security: KMS, audit logs, and SOC2 excerpts for on-prem images
- Canary plan and success criteria

Action items (brief in-header): see action_items field

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): All right hi everyone, thanks for joining, we have about an hour. Quick roll call, and then Carlos will run through the lab repro notes we put together.
[00:07] Priya (Veridian CTO): Thanks, Maya. We pulled in the SRE and PM. We want to make sure this doesn't recur next week when we push the microbatch change.
[00:12] Carlos (Redwood SE): Yep, hi. I'll start by describing what we think happened and what we tried in our sandbox. Spoiler: there's a KV-cache divergence when prefix reuse and partial token eviction happen under the continuous batching path.
[00:25] Daniel (Veridian SRE): Sorry, can you say 'KV-cache divergence' in plain words? We saw duplicated tokens and sometimes the model responded with stale context on retries.
[00:32] Carlos (Redwood SE): Sure — effectively, when a prefix is cached and a subsequent request reuses that cache, if the batcher merges requests and one request gets partially evicted from the local cache due to memory pressure, the runtime can fetch an inconsistent key-value snapshot. So the returned sequence can reflect two different kv-states mid- generation. It's rare but spikes under high concurrency and particular truncation patterns.
[00:54] Priya (Veridian CTO): Ok that matches our incident notes. We saw the big spike at 03:12 UTC when the microbatching change dropped in.
[00:59] Maya (Redwood AE): High level question — is this strictly a runtime bug we need a patch for, or is there a deployment configuration that will mitigate it immediately?
[01:06] Carlos (Redwood SE): Short answer: both. We have a mitigation via stricter eviction thresholds and forcing per-request KV isolation on the path, that reduces the window. But for a long term we should apply a deterministic cache snapshotting fix in the runtime.
[01:19] Lena (Veridian PM): From product side we need to know whether canary is safe to run in our VPC or whether you recommend Dedicated with strict isolation. Also need to know telemetry we should watch.
[01:29] Carlos (Redwood SE): Telemetry — watch per-request KV hits, cache eviction counts, LRU churn, and token timing (time-per-token over the KV fetch). We'll share a dashboard. Also instrumented trace ids we asked for (x-request-id) — that helps correlate.
[01:44] Daniel (Veridian SRE): We uploaded the trace slice to the shared bucket but it's not sanitized. We'll get it cleaned and re-upload. There were some PII traces.
[01:51] Priya (Veridian CTO): On security — we need KMS integration and proof that cache snapshots aren't persisted to disk unencrypted. We are also under SOC2 and need audit log proof.
[02:02] Maya (Redwood AE): Understood. We'll attach the SOC2 excerpt and the KMS integration notes. For Dedicated/Private we provide KMS/HSM hooks and you can keep cache in-memory only (no disk spill) on the deployment template.
[02:15] Carlos (Redwood SE): There's one nuance — on our Hosted tier we do memory-backed caches with optional spill to tmpfs; while Dedicated and Private allow you to disable spill entirely.
[02:27] Daniel (Veridian SRE): Good. For now we prefer a Dedicated canary to isolate variables. Price is a factor though. Maya, can you put together expected delta for burst vs reserved capacity?
[02:37] Maya (Redwood AE): Yep will do. I'll include a 7-day estimate and a one-time canary cost line item.
[02:42] [00:02] Carlos (Redwood SE): Back to repro — steps we recommend: 1) run continuous batching with prefix reuse, 2) seed memory pressure to trigger partial evictions, 3) run a subset of workloads that include streaming and non-streaming calls to exercise both code paths. Our sandbox script is at the shared link.
[02:58] Priya (Veridian CTO): How confident are you the local repro will match our production characteristics? We use 8k seq lengths in the pipeline sometimes.
[03:06] Carlos (Redwood SE): Matches if you replicate tokenization and the sequence-length distribution. The critical factor is the concurrency and the eviction pressure profile. We'll help parameterize the script to match your histograms.
[03:17] Lena (Veridian PM): For the canary, what are the safety nets? Will traffic automatically fallback to the previous model if errors exceed threshold?
[03:24] Carlos (Redwood SE): Yes — Redwood Console supports a canary policy with automatic rollback. You can set failure thresholds (5xx rate or increase in P95) and a circuit breaker that folds traffic back to a safe variant or to a cold path. We'll propose a three-tier fallback: 1) reduce canary fraction, 2) route to Hosted stable model, 3) abort rollout.
[03:41] Daniel (Veridian SRE): We want more granularity on error classification — not all token anomalies are 5xxs. Some are validity regressions e.g., truncated responses. Can the console alert on token-level anomalies?
[03:52] Carlos (Redwood SE): We have a quality rule engine that can do prompt-output checks and count mismatch ratios. We can add a heuristic to flag duplicated tokens or sudden drop in response length. That can emit an event that triggers the rollout circuit.
[04:06] Priya (Veridian CTO): Great. Also, on compliance — we need evidence that audit logs capture model version, rollout id, user id and KMS key access. Is that captured?
[04:15] Maya (Redwood AE): Yep, audit logs include model id, version, rollout id, request metadata and KMS key id for encryption operations. We'll send a sample audit slice.
[04:25] [00:04] Carlos (Redwood SE): Quick demo time — I'm going to share the sandbox run I did last night. (ambient typing) 
[04:35] [screen share audible] Carlos (Redwood SE): Ok here is a run with controlled eviction. You can see at t=215s duplicate tokens emitted on requests with shared prefix. The KV cache hit rate dips right before it happens. I'm stepping through instrumented logs now.
[04:52] Daniel (Veridian SRE): That aligns with our trace — we see a drop in the cache hit fraction right before the error. Is there a way to ensure the cache snapshot is atomic to a request?
[05:00] Carlos (Redwood SE): Yes, the deterministic fix is to snapshot the KV state per-request at read-time — that adds a small CPU/memory overhead but removes the divergence window. For immediate mitigation we recommend bumping the LRU threshold and enabling per-request isolated cache for high-risk routes.
[05:16] Priya (Veridian CTO): Overhead estimate? If we enable per-request snapshots for a subset of paths, what's the expected latency delta?
[05:23] Carlos (Redwood SE): For typical Llama-like models at 512 context it's about 8-15ms median token delta in our tests; for long sequences (4k-8k) it grows proportionally. We'll send a microbenchmark matrix.
[05:35] Maya (Redwood AE): That ties into the cost/delta conversation — we'll provide the numbers and also an option to only snapshot for routes that fail the quality checks.
[05:44] Lena (Veridian PM): For our success criteria, propose: P95 end-to-end latency < 180ms, duplication rate < 0.01% across the canary window, and no unverified 5xx spikes. Can we detect duplication at ingest?
[05:57] Carlos (Redwood SE): Yes we can add a token-dupe detector in the quality pipeline. It'll look for long runs of identical tokens or immediate repetition patterns.
[06:07] Daniel (Veridian SRE): About the canary environment — we prefer Dedicated 4xA100 with KV spill disabled. If that's cost-prohibitive, we can fallback to Hosted with guaranteed tmpfs only.
[06:17] Maya (Redwood AE): I'll outline both options cost-wise. Also note Dedicated will give you the cleanest isolation for the repro.
[06:24] Priya (Veridian CTO): One more required ask: show us the regression test harness and how we'll validate model behavior post-fix. We want to include our internal prompt set in the evaluation.
[06:33] Carlos (Redwood SE): We can run Redwood Optimize evals with your prompt set; we'll version the eval and tie a regression alert to any drop in BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics or custom scoring you provide.
[06:44] Maya (Redwood AE): Ok quick recap and next steps before we wrap.
[06:48] Priya (Veridian CTO): Go ahead.
[06:50] Maya (Redwood AE): 1) Carlos will reproduce the KV divergence on a Dedicated pool and dump the debug traces, target 2025-09-06. 2) Veridian will sanitize/upload the production traces by 2025-09-04. 3) We'll exchange SOC2/KMS docs and a sample audit slice by 2025-09-05. 4) Schedule canary 2025-09-10 with the canary policy we discussed. 5) Redwood to propose rollback thresholds and estimated cost delta by 2025-09-05. Anything to add?
[07:12] Lena (Veridian PM): Please include the exact dashboard panels to watch and the alert mute window so our Ops knows what to expect.
[07:19] Carlos (Redwood SE): Will do, I'll include links to the panels and the exact metric names.
[07:24] Daniel (Veridian SRE): One procedural note — if the canary fails we want an automatic incident ticket created in our PagerDuty. Can we integrate that?
[07:31] Maya (Redwood AE): Yes, we support webhook-based incident triggers that can hit PagerDuty or any ticketing tool. We'll send the integration doc.
[07:37] Priya (Veridian CTO): Thanks all. That gives us a clear path.
[07:40] Maya (Redwood AE): Great, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts and set calendar for the canary. Thanks everyone.
[07:45] [Meeting ends]
